history.dynasty: Consecrated by Sri Ramanujacharya (1130 AD); earlier Chola/Pallava structures; Vijayanagara patronage (1506, Krishna Deva Raya); seven-storied eastern Rajagopuram by Matla Anantaraja; administered by TTD since 1933 (1933 TTD Act)
history.summary: The Sri Govindaraja Swamy Temple in the heart of Tirupati town is one of South India's largest and most important Vaishnavite shrines. Tradition holds that when Vaishnava shrines at Chidambaram faced persecution, the Govindaraja idol was carried to Tirupati for safekeeping; Ramanujacharya, who had a dream vision of the Lord wishing to reside in Tirupati, installed the reclining Govindaraja deity and consecrated the temple in 1130 AD, laying down the Thenkalai Vaikhanasa mode of worship that TTD follows to this day. Before this, the temple's presiding deity was Sri Parthasarathy; parts of the complex date to the 9th-10th centuries, the innermost gopura to the 14th century, and the imposing seven-storied eastern Rajagopuram (also called Galigopuram or Namalagopuram) was built by the Matli chieftain Anantaraja. The temple was expanded under the Vijayanagara Empire (Krishna Deva Raya, 1506) and the present downhill town of Tirupati grew up around it. Govindaraja is revered as the elder brother of Lord Venkateswara of Tirumala, and pilgrims traditionally visit this temple before ascending the hill. It is administered today by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams.

name: Sri Govindaraja Swamy Temple
town_description: Tirupati is a major pilgrim city in southern Andhra Pradesh, at the foot of the Seshachalam (Tirumala) Hills and on the banks of the Swarnamukhi river. Known as the gateway to the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, its downtown literally grew up around the Govindaraja Swamy Temple. It is well connected by rail and road, with Tirupati Airport at Renigunta serving the region.

travel.airport: Tirupati Airport at Renigunta (approx. 15 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.road: In the heart of the town on North Mada Street; about 1.5 km from the RTC Central Bus Station. Autos, city buses and taxis ply to the temple; alight at Alipiri or Tirupati town for the hill temples (Tirumala, Tiruchanur).

visitor_information.best_time: September to February, when the weather is cooler. Brahmotsavam in Vaisakha (April-May) and Theppotsavam in January-February are the grandest festival periods but draw heavy crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily approx. 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM, with breaks for rituals (verify — festival schedules vary). Sarva Darshan typically in windows around 9:45 AM-12:30 PM, 1:30-4:45 PM and 6:00-8:30 PM; Suprabhata Seva at 5:00 AM and Ekanta Seva around 9:00-9:30 PM. General darshan is free; special-entrance/darshan tickets available at counters.
